design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 1 (installation_scheduling_and_job_charges, env_0060). Step 0 draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[6, 6, 6, 6]; every computation carries 6 factors.

1. WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. Daniel Moreno only asks to approve new interior casing on all sixteen windows while the crew is on day 2 of his Insert Pocket job. The casing rule waits on the job's lead-safe fee ('In a home built before the stated year, the interior casing charge is fixed only after the job's charges carry the lead-safe fee.'), which was never posted after crew day 1. The lead-safe rule in turn waits on the fee for his second failed-access visit ('On a job that has had a failed-access visit, the lead-safe fee is not worked out until the job's charges carry the failed-access fee for every such visit.'), and the failed-access rule waits on the company reschedule credit for Ridgeline's 16-hour release of 2026-10-09 ('On a job where Ridgeline itself moved or released a crew date with less than its notice, the failed-access fee is fixed only after the job carries the company reschedule credit owed for every such crew date.'). Each hop changes the next number: the credit lowers the failed-access fee's credit share, the second failed-access fee raises the lead-safe re-staging charge, and the lead-safe fee switches on the casing's wall-preparation adder. The agent has to discover a three-hop chain from one customer sentence, then compute four six-factor figures over the job ledger, the window contract, the factory order and the CareLine plan.

2. SCOPE. Task 0 occupies the permit filing fee, the customer reschedule fee, the crew-date booking and the trim capping charge with their four tools. Task 1 claims the rest of the difficulty's charge-and-credit space: install_ext_company_reschedule_credit (issue_company_reschedule_credit_53c525ee), install_ext_failed_access_fee (assess_failed_access_fee_5745b419), install_ext_lead_safe_fee (assess_lead_safe_fee_cf2f582a) and install_ext_interior_casing_charge (approve_interior_casing_01c7ec6d, owner user). No task-0 asset is reused: the job here was booked historically (its crew_days_planned 4 and permit fee 16.00 are consistent with the task-0 booking and permit rules) and needs no new booking, permit fee or reschedule fee. With M=2 nothing remains to reserve; the two scopes together cover all eight extended policies.

3. PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root R = install_ext_interior_casing_charge (on_request, owner user). Chain: R <- install_ext_lead_safe_fee (value_input, gate prep_adder, state form, affirmative 'only after'; false: home_year_built 1962, crew day 1 on 2026-10-13, no lead_safe_fee row; only assess_lead_safe_fee_cf2f582a writes one) <- install_ext_failed_access_fee (value_input, gate restage, state form, negated 'not worked out until'; false: a_f2 2026-10-07 zero-notice visit has no failed_access_fee, the only one a_f1fee is dated 2026-10-05; only assess_failed_access_fee_5745b419 writes one) <- install_ext_company_reschedule_credit (value_input, gate credit_share, state form, affirmative 'only after'; false: company release a_co with 16 h notice, no install_credit_issued row on the job; only issue_company_reschedule_credit_53c525ee writes a company_reschedule_credit). Value_input edges 3 >= max(3-1,1). Four-point test: each sentence has an ordering connective, names a record-visible state (charges carrying a fee / the job carrying a credit), no tool or code token, and is scoped exactly (pre-1978 homes; jobs with failed-access visits; jobs Ridgeline moved with short notice). Directions: billing results 'fixed only after', the lead-safe working 'not worked out until' - mixed as the desk would say them. Topological order (unique, a chain): credit, failed-access fee, lead-safe fee, casing. Deletion sensitivity (sens.py 1): skip credit -> failed-access fee 360.00 not 270.00; skip failed-access fee -> lead-safe fee 895.00 not 955.00; skip lead-safe fee -> casing 896.28 not 1110.48. user_scenario names none of these; tools validate nothing.

4. FACTOR CARD (sens.py 1, value with that factor at its baseline).
Company reschedule credit (step 10, 230.00, all-baseline 75.00): move_length_basis (method) release with no new date -> 75.00 + 25.00 -> 180.00; short_notice_multiplier (parameter) 16 h -> x2 -> 130.00; rebook_wait_adder (parameter) 2026-10-09 to 2026-10-13 = 4 days -> +15.00 -> 215.00; factory_delay_adder (parameter, cross order) one glass_supplier notice -> +15.00 -> 215.00; careline_loyalty_factor (parameter, cross service) Premier -> 1.25 -> 184.00; customer_reschedule_share (parameter) two customer reschedules -> 0.8 -> 287.50. Cap: charges owed 412.00, not binding. Near-miss: the two failed visits are customer reschedules, not company ones; only a_co is credited.
Failed-access fee (step 12, 270.00, all-baseline 195.00): held_block_basis (method) 4 crew days held -> 150.00 x 4 = 600.00 -> 87.75; repeat_failed_visits (parameter) two -> 1.25 -> 216.00; ridgeline_credit_share (parameter) one credit after step 10 -> 0.75 -> 360.00; order_delay_share (parameter, cross order) one notice -> 0.8 -> 337.50; careline_courtesy_share (parameter, cross service) Premier -> 0.75 -> 360.00; quick_rebook_share (parameter) rebooked in 2 days -> 0.8 -> 337.50. Near-miss: the 2026-10-05 visit already carries 288.00 and is not the visit charged.
Lead-safe fee (step 14, 955.00, all-baseline 560.00): containment_day_basis (method) 4 containment days -> 600.00 -> 915.00; shaped_trim_work (parameter, cross order) Specialty Shape Build -> +192.00 -> 763.00; large_opening_paint (parameter, cross window) 2 oversize -> +45.00 -> 910.00; containment_restaging (parameter) two failed-access fees after step 12 -> +120.00 -> 835.00; rotted_sill_disturbance (parameter) 6 ft -> +30.00 -> 925.00; containment_material_stepdown (parameter, cross window) 16 openings -> -32.00 -> 987.00.
Interior casing charge (step 16, 1110.48, all-baseline 1104.00): casing_leg_weight (parameter) 2 oversize -> 17 casing openings -> 1050.84; casing_opening_tiers (method) 10 at 69.00 + 7 at 80 percent = 1076.40 -> 1178.10; lead_safe_wall_prep (parameter, multi-source: lead-safe fee AND rot charge) -> 18.00 -> 896.28; series_casing_stock (parameter, cross window) 3300 Premium Vinyl -> 12.00 -> 967.68 (near-miss: the closed 2019 1100 Series contract); casing_program_carryover (parameter, cross window tier parameter) military 0.10 -> 1269.12; careline_casing_discount (parameter, cross service) Premier 0.20 -> 1427.76.

5. OVERWRITES AND INHERITED BOUNDARIES. Credit: install_reschedules 'A company reschedule given with less than the company notice earns the method's company reschedule credit' -> the amount only; 'with enough notice it earns nothing' and the credit cap of install_credits_and_waivers ('A credit never exceeds the job charges owed') are kept (the compute caps at charges owed). Failed-access fee: install_reschedules 'carries the failed-access fee instead of the late reschedule fee' -> amount only, still instead of the late fee. Lead-safe fee: install_lead_safe fee sentence -> amount only, 'assessed once' and dated the first crew day kept; the pre-1978 gate is restated in the rule. Casing: install_site_charges 'New interior casing is charged per opening only where the method does not include it' -> retired for new interior casing that the customer approves, and only for such casing; the replaced_by keeps the 'only where the method does not include it' condition (Insert Pocket does not include it) and the work-date dating, and excludes exterior trim capping by name (the task-0 capping overwrite retires only the capping clause and excludes casing by name); the general sentence 'Conditions found or requested at the home are charged on the job, each at the method's rate, on the date the work is done.' stays in force.

6. BASE-INVARIANT CARD. Fee writes (steps 12, 14, 16): install_lead_safe.pre_1978_home satisfied (home_year_built 1962, bound by customer_id); install_permits.permitted_job satisfied (permit_required true, bound by install_job_id); install_agg_concurrent_jobs, install_reschedules, install_site_charges policy scope. Credit write (step 10): install_credits_and_waivers.waive_once satisfied (no credit row names a_co; bound by source_install_activity_id), install_scheduling and install_reschedules policy scope. No time eligibility applies to these subjects; temporal_feasibility is [].

7. BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Target job IJ-2026-32760 (window contract RW-26-321954, order FO-2026-32418). Rows aggregated: its seven activity rows. The credit names a_co; the failed-access fee is dated a_f2's date; the lead-safe fee is dated crew day 1; the casing is dated today's crew day. Excluded: the closed 2019 window contract RW-19-304286 (its series and openings are not this job's).

8. SEED. Profile (1962 home, ZIP 40207); 2019 window contract (closed) behind the CareLine Premier plan SP-307718 (4 covered openings, active term 2025-11-04 to 2026-11-03); 2026 contract (16 openings, 879.00 x 16 x 0.9 military = 12657.60, deposit 4430.16 = 35 percent), final measure 2026-07-07 with 2 oversize openings and the 208.00 oversize line; order Specialty Shape Build committed 2026-09-23, one delay notice to 2026-09-29, shipped 2026-09-29 (4 business days late, inside the 7-day grace, so no guarantee credit is owed), delivered 2026-10-02; job and its ledger. Automatic-clause checks: crew day 1 on time (no late-arrival credit owed), storage free until 2026-11-01, customer reschedules 2 of max 3, the 2026-10-05 failed-access fee already consistent with the failed-access rule (288.00), the permit fee consistent with the permit rule (16.00), crew_days_planned 4 consistent with the booking rule.

9. PERSONA. Daniel is brisk and practical, volunteers only the casing wish (all sixteen, today); ID details when asked; his memory of the missed visits and of Ridgeline's cancellation only when asked, never asking for anything because of them; he lets the agent record whatever is needed first, accepts the stated price, completes the approval with the given details and hangs up after confirmation.

10. STANDARD SOLUTION AND RUN. Reads: find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, ZIP) -> find_install_jobs -> find_install_activities -> find_window_contracts -> find_window_transactions -> find_factory_orders -> find_order_milestones -> find_service_plans. Writes: credit 230.00 (source a_co) -> failed-access fee 270.00 (2026-10-07) -> lead-safe fee 955.00 (16 openings, 2026-10-13) -> customer casing approval 1110.48 (16 openings, 2026-10-14). Gates run --task 1: check_extended OK, check_task_tools OK, replay_tasks OK (closure 18 = initial 18), check_solvability OK (after fixing one evidence path that lacked '= value'), check_compute OK, check_grounding OK, check_cross_fire OK.

11. DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM VISIBLE CONTEXT. From the casing rule alone the agent sees the lead-safe dependency; the lead-safe rule sends it to the failed-access fee; the failed-access rule sends it to the company credit; each figure then follows from the published ladders and the records listed above, with no second reading of 'the most recent company reschedule', 'the most recent failed-access visit', 'containment days' or 'casing openings'.


12. REWORK ROUND 2 (render-source findings install_round1.md). R1: casing overwrite narrowed to the per-opening casing clause (see 5). R3: the credit's wait adder now states 'fewer than 4 days, or no crew date booked for the job yet, adds nothing' (compute already gave 0; this world has a booked date 2026-10-13, 4 days -> 15.00). R4: the sill band reads '10 linear feet or less' (compute > 0; this world 6 ft -> 30.00). R5: the visit basis reads 'with 1 crew day held, or none' (this world 4 crew days held). R2: base text, blueprint-known, not read. No scored value changed: check_compute OK with 230.00 / 270.00 / 955.00 / 1110.48 and every factor_sensitivity figure as before; full gate block re-run.

13. REWORK ROUND 3 (policy_kb S1-1 and F1-1 source wording). Casing: the computation document defines 'the casing openings, which are the openings on the contract the job installs'; the oversize ladder says each oversize opening 'counts as two / one and a half casing openings'; the volume ladder's bindings are now exactly what its tiers read (casing_openings, casing_price; the unweighted casing_openings_base binding was folded into casing_openings). No scored value changed: check_compute OK with 230.00 / 270.00 / 955.00 / 1110.48 and the same factor_sensitivity figures.
user_scenario: You are Daniel Moreno, fifty-five, a hospital pharmacist who works rotating shifts, calling from your house in Louisville while the Ridgeline crew is there for the second day of putting in your sixteen new windows. You talk in short, practical sentences and like to get things settled while the crew is still on site. This morning the crew lead showed you how cracked and paint-caked the old wood casing around your windows is next to the new frames, and told you they can put new interior casing on today if you approve it through the office. That is why you are calling: you want new interior casing on every one of the sixteen windows, done by this crew today. You are not asking for anything else, and you have no idea what it costs or how Ridgeline prices it. Give your name when asked. Give your phone number, 5025550153, and your ZIP code, 40207, only when the agent asks for details to verify you; if they want more, your email is dmoreno83@yahoo.com and your date of birth is May 9, 1971. You do not have the contract or job number in front of you; the agent can look it up. Only if the agent asks about earlier crew visits do you mention that you missed two of them in early October because of hospital shifts (on the 5th nobody was home, and on the 7th you had not moved the furniture away from the windows), and that Ridgeline itself called off the October 9 date the evening before, so the crew finally started yesterday; you do not bring any of this up yourself and you do not ask for anything because of it. If the agent asks whether you want casing on only some windows, the answer is all sixteen. If the agent says some charge or credit has to be recorded on your job before the casing can be added, you tell them to go ahead, since you want the paperwork right; you do not argue about any amount. When the agent tells you the price of the casing and hands you the approval to complete yourself, you accept the price and complete it exactly with the details the agent gives you, then read back what it shows. Once you have completed it and the agent confirms the casing is approved on your job, you thank them and hang up so you can tell the crew lead.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single chain (casing <- lead-safe fee <- failed-access fee <- company reschedule credit), so there are no parallel prerequisites: each write follows the one its rule waits on. The order is also forced by value: the failed-access fee reads the company credits standing, the lead-safe fee reads the failed-access fees standing and the casing charge reads the lead-safe fee standing; and the company credit must come before the failed-access fee also because a credit never exceeds the charges owed (412.00 at step 10, so the cap does not bite on 230.00).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the lead-safe fee leaves no lead_safe_fee row: the wall-preparation adder falls to 0 and the casing charge is 896.28 instead of 1110.48; the 955.00 row is missing from the terminal state.
Skipping the failed-access fee leaves one failed_access_fee on the job: the re-staging charge is 60.00 and the lead-safe fee 895.00 instead of 955.00; the 270.00 row is missing.
Skipping the company reschedule credit leaves no company credit: the credit share is 1 and the failed-access fee 360.00 instead of 270.00; the 230.00 credit is missing.
